correctness.rationale: The hyperboloid proof reconstructs the support optimization without using a finite experiment as an infinite proof. For a support normal \(n\), the vertex pairings \(s_i=\langle v_i,n\rangle\) are nonnegative and the maximum hyperbolic distance is attained at a vertex because projective barycentric normalization only increases the Lorentz denominator. Inverting the regular-simplex Gram matrix gives the exact normalization \(1=(q-1)^{-1}(\sum s_i^2-\frac{q}{dq+1}(\sum s_i)^2)\). After dividing by \(M=\max s_i\), minimizing width is equivalent to maximizing a strictly convex quadratic on a union of cube faces. Hence a maximizer is a zero-one pattern. With exactly \(k\) ones the objective is \(F_k=k((d-k)q+1)/(dq+1)\), and the consecutive difference has the stated sign, uniquely maximizing at \(k=\lceil d/2\rceil\). This proves both the closed thickness formula and the complete minimizer classification. The package verifier independently checks the Gram inverse, the difference identity and the tetrahedral specialization.
